result.title: RefCloth: Transferable Adversarial Tablecloths for Vision-Language-Action Models
result.summary: Closed-loop vision-language-action (VLA) policies rely continuously on multi-view cameras, yet existing visual attacks typically hijack sensor streams with 2D patches or alter target object meshes that require retraining when manipulation objects change. We introduce RefCloth, a framework that optimizes one persistent adversarial tablecloth on a frozen source policy and deploys it zero-shot across unseen tasks and target models without modifying task objects or cameras. Throughout manipulation, static third-person and moving wrist views observe this shared world-bound texture under evolving occlusions. To generalize across shifting surface views while bridging the gap between differentiable and native renderers, RefCloth combines bounded texture parameterization with shared surface UV transformations and a same-path clean reference that removes static rendering offsets at initialization. Across four LIBERO suites in native simulation, one frozen texture transfers from OpenVLA-OFT to $π_0$ and $π_{0.5}$, reducing success relative to an unoptimized cloth by 62.50 and 43.75 percentage points on average and far exceeding amplitude- and variation-matched random controls. Dual-view audits and target closed-loop camera interventions show that moving wrist exposure drives over twice the standalone drop of the main view with strong synergy, while ablations confirm the roles of UV diversification and path calibration.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 RefCloth，在冻结源策略上优化一张持久的对抗桌布，结合有界纹理参数化、共享表面 UV 变换与同路径干净参考，使其零样本迁移到未见任务和 π0、π0.5 等目标 VLA，并在 LIBERO 上验证攻击效果。
AI.relevance_reason: 其双视角遮挡审计与相机干预显示腕部视角对失败贡献更大，可供核查 LVR 中视觉证据选择、视觉旁路与多视角信息使用的诊断思路，但论文本身不涉及 latent 推理状态。
